title: B12 deficiency: subacute combined degeneration (dorsal columns + lateral corticospinal)
vignette: A 54-year-old woman is evaluated in the clinic due to easy fatigability. The patient has had no weight gain or cold intolerance and has no history of thyroid conditions. Medical history is significant for gastrectomy due to a nonhealing gastric ulcer. Physical examination shows a shiny tongue and pale palmar creases. The patient's gait is unstable when her eyes are closed, and vibration sense is decreased in the upper and lower extremities. There is mild, symmetric loss of strength affecting the proximal lower extremity muscles. Blood hemoglobin level is 7.2 g/dL and white blood cell count is 3,600/mm3. Stool tests for occult blood are repeatedly negative. The spinal cord cross-sections show five patterns of involvement (A-E); pattern D highlights the dorsal columns together with the lateral corticospinal tracts. Which of the following spinal cord regions is most likely to be affected by this patient's disease process?

clues.text: gastrectomy due to a nonhealing gastric ulcer
clues.note: Gastrectomy removes intrinsic factor-producing parietal cells, causing vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency over time.

clues.text: shiny tongue and pale palmar creases
clues.note: Atrophic glossitis (shiny tongue) and pallor of anemia are features of B12 deficiency (megaloblastic anemia).

clues.text: gait is unstable when her eyes are closed
clues.note: A positive Romberg sign (unsteady with eyes closed) indicates DORSAL COLUMN dysfunction (loss of proprioception) - part of subacute combined degeneration.
Loss of vibration/position sense localizes to the DORSAL COLUMNS, damaged in B12 deficiency.

whatMatters: Post-gastrectomy vitamin B12 deficiency (megaloblastic anemia + neurologic signs) causes SUBACUTE COMBINED DEGENERATION: demyelination of the DORSAL COLUMNS (loss of vibration/position sense, positive Romberg), the LATERAL CORTICOSPINAL tracts (weakness/spastic paresis), and spinocerebellar tracts (ataxia). The cross-section highlighting the dorsal columns + lateral corticospinal tracts is pattern D. Answer D.
strategy: Recognize B12 deficiency (post-gastrectomy, megaloblastic anemia, glossitis) with combined DORSAL COLUMN (sensory ataxia, Romberg) and CORTICOSPINAL (weakness) signs = subacute combined degeneration. Pick the cross-section involving BOTH dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts. Reject anterior-horn (polio/SMA - flaccid, no sensory loss), random white matter (MS), dorsal columns + dorsal root ganglia (tabes dorsalis), and central cord (syringomyelia).

options.text: Dorsal columns and dorsal root ganglia
Dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts

eliminations.label: Anterior horns - poliomyelitis/spinal muscular atrophy
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: destruction of anterior-horn (lower motor) neurons = poliomyelitis or spinal muscular atrophy. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes FLACCID paralysis, atrophy, and fasciculations WITHOUT sensory loss - not the sensory (dorsal column) findings here. ✅ Correct if: pure lower motor neuron weakness with fasciculations.

eliminations.label: Random white matter patches - multiple sclerosis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: inflammatory demyelination in a random, asymmetric pattern = multiple sclerosis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: MS lesions are disseminated in space/time in a young adult, not the symmetric dorsal-column + corticospinal pattern of B12 deficiency. ✅ Correct if: relapsing focal CNS deficits in a young woman.

eliminations.label: Dorsal columns + dorsal root ganglia - tabes dorsalis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: degeneration of dorsal columns AND dorsal root ganglia = tabes dorsalis (tertiary neurosyphilis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: tabes affects sensory pathways/ganglia (with Argyll Robertson pupils) but spares the lateral corticospinal tracts and doesn't cause megaloblastic anemia. ✅ Correct if: neurosyphilis with lancinating pains and Argyll Robertson pupils.

eliminations.label: Central cord - syringomyelia (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a central cavitation damaging the crossing spinothalamic fibers (anterior white commissure) = syringomyelia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes a 'cape' distribution loss of pain/temperature, not the dorsal-column + corticospinal degeneration of B12 deficiency. ✅ Correct if: bilateral loss of pain/temperature over the shoulders/arms.

reasoning: Post-gastrectomy loss of intrinsic factor -> vitamin B12 deficiency (megaloblastic anemia + glossitis)
B12 deficiency damages myelin, causing subacute combined degeneration
This involves the dorsal columns (sensory ataxia, positive Romberg) AND the lateral corticospinal tracts (weakness/spasticity)
-> cross-section with dorsal columns + lateral corticospinal tracts; answer D
mechanism: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a cofactor for methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase; deficiency (here from gastrectomy removing intrinsic factor) causes megaloblastic anemia (elevated homocysteine and methylmalonic acid). Accumulated methylmalonic acid and impaired methylation destabilize MYELIN, damaging the large myelinated tracts of the spinal cord - SUBACUTE COMBINED DEGENERATION. The affected tracts are the DORSAL COLUMNS (loss of vibration and position sense -> sensory ataxia and a positive Romberg sign), the LATERAL CORTICOSPINAL tracts (upper motor neuron weakness/spastic paresis), and the spinocerebellar tracts (contributing to ataxia). Patients also develop atrophic glossitis (shiny tongue) and pallor from anemia. On a spinal cord cross-section, the pattern involves BOTH the dorsal columns and the lateral corticospinal tracts (pattern D). The distractors localize elsewhere: anterior horns (polio/SMA), random white matter (MS), dorsal columns + dorsal root ganglia (tabes dorsalis), and central cord (syringomyelia).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro/Heme > B12 deficiency subacute combined degeneration: dorsal columns (vibration/position, Romberg), lateral corticospinal (weakness/spasticity), spinocerebellar (ataxia); megaloblastic anemia; MMA/homocysteine up.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Combined dorsal-column + corticospinal signs from B12 deficiency = pattern D on the cord cross-section.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on subacute combined degeneration, dorsal columns, lateral corticospinal tract, Romberg sign, or intrinsic factor? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Anterior horn (polio/SMA), MS (random), tabes dorsalis (dorsal columns + ganglia), syringomyelia (central) are different cord patterns.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the cord cross-sections: pattern D highlights the POSTERIOR (dorsal) columns AND the LATERAL corticospinal tracts bilaterally. Anchor: 'B12 = dorsal columns + lateral corticospinal (± spinocerebellar) = combined degeneration.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: B12 deficiency -> subacute combined degeneration (dorsal columns + lateral corticospinal + spinocerebellar); check MMA + homocysteine.

memoryHook: B12 keeps myelin intact; lose it after a gastrectomy and the cord's big highways rot - dorsal columns (wobble with eyes shut) plus corticospinal (stiff-weak legs) = subacute combined degeneration.
